[i][b]Proposition of a formal alliance to [nation]Valddera[/nation] - TV Ad break News - Naerim, Tirakan[/b][/i]

[i]*a quick intro signal the beginning of the ad-break-breaking-news-programm*[/i]

Shortly after Premier Arlan Vos re-election victory speech, the Tiraki government confirmed that it has formally stated its intention to declare a strategic alliance with Valddera, based on common goals and shared culture. Officials stated that Tirakan views Valddera as a natural partner in the region and is now awaiting a response from Valddera's government. Later the same day, Premier Vos addressed reporters questions in the Golden Office.

[i]*a video of Arlan Vos sitting in the Golden Office next to the Minister of Foreign Affairs blends in*[/i]

"Look, people ask me all the time, why Valddera? And it's a fair question. A very fair question. But the answer is actually very simple.
Valddera and Tirakan think alike. We do. We really do. Politically, culturally, strategically, theres alignment there, real alignment. We both believe in sovereignty. We both believe in stability. We both believe that our region should be shaped by the people who live here, not by distant powers who show up when it suits them and disappear when it doesn't.
Culturally, there's a lot of respect. There's a lot of history. There's a lot of understanding. You don't build alliances on paper, you build them on shared heart. And Valddera has that heart. They understand order, they understand responsibility, and the need to protect what your home.
Internationally, our interests overlap in a very big way. Security in the Shamat Sea. Security on East Shamat. Security beyond our region. Trade routes that stay open. Terrorism that gets confronted, not excused. Economic growth that actually benefits our people instead of draining them. On all of that, all of it, we're on the same page. We've seen it. We've seen it many times actually.
We respect Valddera as an equal. We respect their decisions, their leadership. And we think a formal alliance would bring stability, predictability, a lot of that, yes, and strength to the entire region. A lot of strength. Frankly, it's the kind of alliance that benefits the people, and those are the best ones.
So yes, we've made our position clear. The door is open. The offer is serious. And we expect a serious response. Because when Tirakan extends its hand, when it sees long-term value. And Valddera? That value is absolutely there."

[i]*the video fades out again*[/i]

And with that, the focus now shifts from speeches to responses. Tirakan has made its intentions clear, and the coming days will show whether Valddera is ready to match that momentum. Experts say, what follows could be the beginning of a new power structure on East Shamat. For now, the questions remain open, and the answers are expected soon. Thank you for tuning in with us!

[i]*a short outro ends the program and ads cut in*[/i]

[i][b]The Express - DELEGATION TO [nation]Nordiheim[/nation]. ANOTHER ALLIANCE ON IT'S WAY? - Naerim, Tirakan[/b][/i]

Freshly elected Premier Vos, Foreign Relations Minister Vosar Renul, the Minister of Economics Biran Nadir, and several members of parliament from the governing TUP concluded a state visit to the Nordiheimian capital, Midgard, today, founding what Mr. Vos described as a new phase of deeper friendship and strategic alignment between the two countries.

The Tirakani delegation was formally received by Nordiheim's Minister of Midland Siggurd Haraldson, Minister of Vestland Omeo Jarlisen, Minister of Sorland Jiemba Turidson, Minister of War Thormod Thormodson III and Minister of Rites Jannali Idundotir. The visit included a bilateral meeting and a joint press appearance, accompanied by public handshake photographs that gave to show the cordial atmosphere. Officials on both sides emphasized continuity in relations, noting that cooperation between Nordiheim and Tirakan had remained constructive even during Tirakan's years of civil war.
Speaking after the press conference, Premier Vos said discussions focused on trade facilitation and long-term economic planning. He highlighted what he called a "rare degree of alignment" between the two governments, which he only knew from his direct neighbours. "We believe we already trade well," Vos stated, "but we also believe we can do it better than anyone else when we put in the work together."
Foreign Relations Minister Renul echoed the sentiment, pointing to shared approaches on logistics and industrial supply chains. He noted that Tirakan had proposed a framework for strategic cooperation that would go beyond conventional trade agreements, the exact meaning though, seems ambiguous. According to Renul, the proposal builds on "a relationship that existed long before the civil war and proved to last under pressure, which is what we seek."
While no binding agreements were signed during the visit, the government confirmed that follow-up talks would begin in the coming weeks to form the discussions into concrete arrangements.

The visit is widely seen as part of Premier Vos' just shortly ago announced broader effort to reassert itself as a central economic actor beyond Shamat, following reunification. As one senior official put it, the proposal is just the beginning of a win streak. The impact of said win streak on the Tiraki population was framed as benefitial to the common good, but is yet criticized by experts and many members of the parliament, calling out Premier Vos' way of diplomacy as aggressive and unthoughtful. The truth behind these words, is expected to be revealed over the course of 2028.
